provider.notes: NAVER Cloud Platform CLOVA speech recognition. The vendor has no model parameter; its four speech-to-text products are chosen by endpoint and credential type, so the row keys are gateway-defined product aliases (csr, clova-speech-short, clova-speech-long, clova-speech-streaming) and an empty model resolves to csr. Only CSR is implemented, and today's client never reads the session's model, so every NAVER session reaches CSR (gateway/src/core/stt/naver_clova/config.rs:276-334). The client registered today (gateway/src/core/stt/naver_clova/client.rs) buffers the whole call and uploads after 60 s of audio, at hang-up, or when the client sends audio_end (which disconnects and reconnects the speech-to-text client, gateway/src/core/voice_manager/manager.rs:1648-1672). It is not a transport: when_unusable on each row records what a live session gets from it. It also fails badly: after one failed upload it never clears its buffer, so every later audio frame is refused with an error and copies the 1.9 MB buffer again, even while the breaker is open (client.rs:117-120, :152 and :354-360; gateway/src/handlers/ws/audio_handler.rs:130-133). Only the 'csr' row and the default row describe an endpoint that today's credentials can reach: the key must have the form client_id|client_secret (gateway/src/core/stt/naver_clova/config.rs:283-298). The three CLOVA Speech rows need a different credential (a per-domain secret, and for long-sentence recognition a per-domain address) that this configuration cannot carry. Three of the four products are file-only at the vendor and their file endpoints answer in one request, so segmentation is both required and feasible; only CSR is placed in a release (decisions section 12). The vendor's minimum sample rate is 16 kHz. Aliases: the registry accepts naver_clova, naverclova, naver, clova, csr and two Korean spellings (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1788-1791); the standardized factory omits one Korean spelling (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:439).

gateway_client.notes: CLOVA Speech Recognition (CSR): POST https://naveropenapi.apigw.ntruss.com/recog/v1/stt?lang=<Kor|Eng|Jpn|Chn>, raw file body, text-only response. transcribe_buffer already builds this request and can be lifted into the adapter. The adapter must: always wrap PCM in a WAV container and always send Content-Type application/octet-stream (the vendor rejects any other content type and lists no raw PCM format; today the client sends headerless PCM by default and audio/wav or audio/mpeg otherwise, client.rs:136-140, config.rs:147-153); resample to 16 kHz, the vendor minimum (the constructor rejects lower session rates, config.rs:369-374); keep uploads longer than 400 ms (min_audio_ms is an exclusive bound), under 60 s and under 3 MB; treat the vendor's HTTP 500 for unreadable audio as a request fault so one bad upload does not open the breaker shared by all sessions; and report confidence as unknown instead of the hard-coded 1.0 (client.rs:349). The quota in limits.rates is per console application and adjustable; HTTP 429 means it is used up. The legacy client reports every HTTP 413 as 'Audio too long (max 60 seconds)' (client.rs:197-199), although the vendor answers 413 both for audio over 60 s and for a body over 3 MB; the adapter should tell the two apart by the vendor's error code.

segment_profile.rationale: Only the HTTP request timeout deviates from the gateway defaults. 10000 ms is the vendor audit's starting value, not a measurement: no latency is published for any NAVER file API, and the legacy client allows 30 s (gateway/src/core/stt/naver_clova/client.rs:54-58). Replace it with measured P99 plus a margin. The other defaults fit: a 25 s segment with 400 ms pre-roll and 500 ms trailing silence is 25.9 s and about 829 kB as 16 kHz WAV, inside 60 s and 3 MB, and the default padding keeps every upload above the 400 ms minimum. Because every request is billed in 15 s units (billing.increment_ms), segments of the same turn that are still queued should be merged while the merged upload stays within 15 s. An upload must never be held back to wait for a merge, so upload_policy stays at the default (upload at each pause). Calls that arrive at 8 kHz must be upsampled to 16 kHz before upload.

gateway_client.notes: POST {InvokeURL}/recognizer/upload, multipart form with the file and a JSON parameter block, header X-CLOVASPEECH-API-KEY. The vendor's default is an asynchronous job; setting completion=sync makes the same request block and return the result, which is the mode a live call must use and the mode LiveKit's Clova plugin uses. It is the only NAVER file API that returns confidence (overall and per segment, 0 to 1) and word times. For short segments switch off the defaults that add work: speaker diarization, noise filtering and word alignment are all on by default. Languages ko-KR, en-US, enko (mixed), ja, zh-cn, zh-tw. Telephone-network codecs are not supported; convert to 16 kHz mono PCM first. The asynchronous mode (token, then polling) must not be used on calls.

gateway_client.notes: Bidirectional gRPC; first message is a JSON configuration, then audio chunks. Audio must be headerless PCM, 16 kHz, mono, 16-bit. Languages ko, en, ja only (no Chinese). Basic long-sentence plan only. At most 15 connections per domain and a 5-minute connection lifetime, so the client must reconnect within a call. The vendor decides where a chunk ends through its 'semanticEpd' settings (gapThreshold in milliseconds of silence, durationThreshold, syllableThreshold, usePeriodEpd, useWordEpd) and emits one result per chunk with confidence and per-word alignment; no unstable partial results are documented, hence interim_results 'none'. vendor_turn_signal records 'unknown', which turn-taking treats as silence: the one mechanism the evidence establishes is the silence gap, and nothing shows that the punctuation and word rules amount to a semantic end-of-turn decision. Recording 'semantic' would let turn-taking trust the vendor's cut more than the evidence allows. The concurrent_sessions entry of limits.rates is the per-domain connection cap.

gateway_client.notes: Same RPC as stream_naver_clova. The client sets epFlag=true with a non-zero seqId in a data request to force the server to recognise what it has buffered and tag the result; without it the server waits for its own end-point rules or for 10 s without requests. Whether the vendor's own end-pointing can be switched off while the gateway drives the flush is not documented. Same connection limits as stream_naver_clova.
